nodes.description: Purified TRAF7 coiled-coil fragments form trimers. p.Lys346Glu reduces the apparent molecular weight and stability of this assembly, whereas p.Arg371Gly showed no significant molecular-weight change. Both variants failed to rescue Traf7 knockdown in zebrafish; the shared rescue failure does not demonstrate a shared trimer defect or dominant-negative mechanism.

evidence.snippet: MALS assays revealed that K346E exhibited a lower molecular weight compared to the wild-type TRAF7 CC, while R371G did not present a significant difference in molecular weight (Figure 5B), suggesting a weakened stability of the TRAF7 homotrimer caused by the K346E mutation.

nodes.description: RNA sequencing compared skin fibroblasts from three patients with p.Leu402Val, p.Leu519Phe or p.Arg655Gln against six controls, with and without TNF stimulation. There were 76 differentially expressed genes at baseline and 90 after TNF under the stringent differential-expression threshold. Pathway enrichment used a separate, less stringent set of 726 baseline genes and suggested axon-guidance, Wnt/calcium and NFAT-related pathways. A fourth patient was included in selected qPCR validation; these exploratory findings do not prove that a particular pathway causes the clinical abnormalities.

nodes.description: The developmental syndrome is associated predominantly with recurrent heterozygous missense variants in the WD40 repeats, with some coiled-coil variants also established. The variant spectrum favors allele-specific altered function over simple haploinsufficiency, but does not establish a single biochemical mechanism for every allele. Constitutional and postzygotic mosaic presentations are reported.

evidence.reference_title: TRAF7 in signaling and disease: emerging mechanisms and clinical implications.
evidence.snippet: TRAF7 syndrome is caused by several pathogenic TRAF7 mutations, most of which are located within the WD40 repeat protein domain, and the most recurrent of these mutations are p.Arg655Gln, p.Arg524Trp, and p.Phe617Leu

evidence.reference_title: The spectrum of heart defects in the TRAF7-related multiple congenital anomalies-intellectual disability syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Variants are predominantly within the WD40 repeats and recurrent, suggesting specific alterations to the protein as the pathomechanism, as opposed to haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic spectrum and transcriptomic profile associated with germline variants in TRAF7.
evidence.snippet: The finding of recurrent missense variants largely restricted to the WD40 repeats suggests a disease mechanism involving specific functional changes to the mutant TRAF7 protein, rather than haploinsufficiency.

genetic_context.description: This node describes constitutional heterozygous missense variants, predominantly de novo. A dominant-negative effect is a proposed mechanism rather than an established property of all syndrome alleles; mosaic presentations are described separately in genetics and inheritance.

nodes.description: Traf7 depletion in fish and frog alters neural crest markers and pharyngeal arches. Overexpression of selected developmental variants also perturbs neural crest markers in Xenopus. This is a proposed route to craniofacial and cardiac abnormalities, supported by experimental embryology rather than by lineage tracing in patients. It does not establish a neural-crest origin for developmental delay or digital anomalies.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, TRAF7 knockdown by unilateral injection of morpholinos at the 2-cell stage disrupted the expression of neural crest markers Sox10 and Twist on the injected side (Fig. 2 O and Q).

nodes.description: The discovery study measured reduced ERK1/2 phosphorylation in cells overexpressing syndrome-associated variants. Effects differ by allele: the coiled-coil variants had no or smaller effects than the WD40 variants. These are overexpression results, not measurements in patient-derived fibroblasts. Their relationship to the fibroblast transcriptome and to specific clinical findings is unresolved.

evidence.snippet: Tokita et al reported two TRAF7 syndrome patients with variants in the coiled-coil domain (p.(Lys346Glu) and p.(Arg371Gly)), although these had no or less negative effect on ERK1/2 phosphorylation compared to the two WD40 repeat variants they identified (p.(Thr601Ala) and p.(Arg655Gln)).

nodes.description: Coimmunoprecipitation in HEK293 cells showed reduced IFT57 binding for p.Thr601Ala, the disputed CHD-associated p.Val442Met, and somatic tumor-associated p.Gly536Ser. The p.Thr601Ala experiment supplies a direct connection to the established developmental syndrome. These selected alleles do not establish a universal effect of all germline variants.

evidence.snippet: Meningioma and CHD- and craniofacial defect-associated TRAF7 mutants (G536S, V442M, and T601A, respectively) show reduced interaction with IFT57.

nodes.description: Expression of p.Thr601Ala or p.Val442Met reduced primary cilia in O9 neural crest cells. In frog and fish depletion models, ciliary transport, cilium number and motility were impaired. These findings support a ciliary mechanism for selected alleles; patient-wide ciliary dysfunction has not been demonstrated.
